title: Raiders QB competition: Kirk Cousins has clear edge over Fernando Mendoza - CBS Sports
description: Klint Kubiak says the competition will continue, but Cousins has done little to lose his grip on the starting job
body:
Klint Kubiak says the competition will continue, but Cousins has done little to lose his grip on the starting job
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:02 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With the start of the regular season just over three weeks away, the Las Vegas Raiders still haven't named a starting quarterback. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak had the chance to name a starter following the team's 22-20 preseason win over the Texans on Thursday night, but instead, he decided to keep everyone guessing. "We got another week of playing. I don't want anyone to be comfortable in their job," Kubiak said. "It should always be that way for all positions. So, let's keep going forward."That makes it sound like the battle between Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza will be raging on for another week, but based on what Kubiak has said throughout training camp, it seems like his decision has already been made; he's just not ready to share it. 
Who the Raiders starting QB will likely be in Week 1Right now, all signs point to Cousins. Over the course of training camp, the closest Kubiak has come to naming a starter came after the Raiders' first preseason game back on Aug. 13. In a 27-14 loss to the Cardinals, Cousins was on the field for exactly one offensive possession, and he was nearly perfect: The veteran quarterback went 5-of-6 for 50 yards and a touchdown. "Kirk's been getting the reps with the ones. I think he's had a solid training camp and it's his job to lose," Kubiak said.Those last five words are the key ones: It's his job to lose. In the week since those comments were made, Cousins hasn't really done anything to lose the job. 
The four-time Pro Bowler didn't play on Thursday night against the Texans, but he took part in a joint practice against Houston earlier this week. Cousins put together an up-and-down day against the Texans. On the negative side, he threw a pick-six to Kamari Lassiter, according to The Athletic, but he also made several big plays against a Texans team that will almost certainly have one of the best defenses in the NFL this year. "Probably would have liked to have finished a little stronger," Cousins said after Tuesday's practice, via The Athletic. "But we made some plays in the first few periods that we were pleased with, and we'll keep building from here."With Cousins struggling some, this could have been a spot where Mendoza closed the gap with the 38-year-old veteran, but instead, the No. 1 overall pick also struggled against Houston's defense. During the joint practice, Mendoza actually got some reps with the first team, which has been a rarity for him in training camp, but he wasn't able to outplay Cousins. Mendoza did make some highlight throws, but he also threw two interceptions during a red zone period, including a pick-six to Jalen Pitre, according to The Athletic. 
Although Cousins wasn't on the field for Thursday's preseason game, Mendoza was and the rookie got off to a rough start with a pick-six on his third pass of the game. 
Mendoza ended up finishing 8-of-15 for 86 yards, but the only touchdown he threw went to the other team. After the game, Kubiak said the rookie still has a lot to work on. "Plenty to clean up. Plenty to get better at," Kubiak said when asked about Mendoza's performance. "Plenty that we can do better for him as coaches. Plenty that he can learn from."
With Mendoza facing a steep learning curve, it doesn't seem like he's done enough to take the job from Cousins. Kubiak said it was Cousins' job to lose, and if that's the case, it doesn't seem like he's done enough to lose it. Cousins likely won't play in the Raiders' final preseason game, which means he'll have been on the field for only one series over three games. Most coaches keep their veteran QB on the bench like that to keep their guy healthy for the season, which is another sign the Raiders will probably roll with Cousins in their opener against the Dolphins. Since the start of training camp, there's only been one instance in which Kubiak referred to Cousins as the starter, and that came on Day 1, July 28. 
"When we go out to practice tomorrow, Kirk Cousins is the starting quarterback," Kubiak said. "He's the guy, and he's going to get a ton of reps. He deserves them because he's played really good football. But I want Fernando and I want Aidan (O'Connell) to push him."The depth chart hasn't changed much at quarterback since that day, which is why "Kirk Cousins is the starting quarterback" is something we'll probably hear Kubiak say again in the very near future.

title: Why these five NFL bottom dweller teams still have hope for 2026 season - CBS Sports
description: Even if a Super Bowl isn't in the cards, these six struggling franchises have plenty of young talent and schemati
body:
Even if a Super Bowl isn't in the cards, these six struggling franchises have plenty of young talent and schematic changes worth cheering for this season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:54 am ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With the NFL season getting started in less than a month, all the prognostication and debate have centered on which teams can win the Super Bowl and how high their ceilings are. Conversely, down at the bottom of the NFL, all the hopes lie in the 2027 NFL Draft and the potential of adding players like Texas QB Arch Manning, Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith or South Carolina EDGE Dylan Stewart.However, I'm in the business of optimism, and having been through a lot of bad Jacksonville Jaguars seasons, there are hopeful things you can pull from the muck and mire of a lost season. So, using DraftKings Sportsbook Super Bowl odds, we're going to highlight the six teams with the lowest Super Bowl odds, and give out one reason for optimism and hope among what could be a lost season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Growth from a young coreNow, there's not a lot that's going well for the Cardinals, especially being in a division with the defending Super Bowl champions and the favorites to win the whole thing this season. Despite that, I do think that there's some young talent on the Cardinals' roster that's just waiting to grow and develop with another year in the NFL under their belt.Offensively, head coach/primary playcaller Mike LaFleur inherited a group that is talented but inconsistent in major spots. While the group won't have promising rookie guard Chase Bisontis for the whole season (torn MCL) and first-round RB Jeremiyah Love is currently injured (high ankle sprain), count me as someone who is. … curious about their offense going into the season. 
Last year, I thought the Cardinals' offense had a good foundation, but it was too static and asked their guys to just go and win on islands. Their motion rate of 43.9% was 30th in the NFL, despite being 12th in Offensive Success Rate when a player goes in motion. Now, I'm not of the belief that adding motion into every offense is some magical "Football Flex Seal" that'll make your offense shine, but it will give players such as WRs Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson a much easier chance of creating space, while giving your QB easier answers to the test. It'll especially help Harrison, who is a smooth mover and glider when defensive backs can't get their hands on him at the line of scrimmage. LaFleur using more motion and easier ways of getting his young stars the ball should help them grow in a big way, and that's exciting for 2026.Flipping it, I think the defense has talent in important spots when healthy. DT Walter Nolen III is a game wrecker with his speed and explosiveness, and CB Will Johnson had promising moments, but neither player can stay healthy for long (Nolen played in six games and Johnson played in 12). If you get healthy years from those two, combined with quality reps from EDGE Josh Sweat, CB Garrett Williams and S Budda Baker, you get a fun core that should be built around moving forward.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Your hipster friend's favorite offenseThe 2026 Miami Dolphins should be a pain in the butt for backside EDGEs to defend. New offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik goes about his business differently than former playcaller Mike McDaniel, but both come from the same San Francisco tree, where forcing defenses into base defense via heavy personnel is the way to go. Where I think this can help Miami, and QB Malik Willis is leaning into the athleticism of their offensive stars, which should make for some fun moments. Left tackle Patrick Paul, left guard Kadyn Proctor, center Aaron Brewer, and RB De'Von Achane are all good athletes who fit the offense Slowik is bringing to Miami. Combine that with Willis being a run threat to backside EDGEs, and you (potentially) get cutback lanes galore. Let's see if the Dolphins are interested in running the triple option.
Does this mean I think the Dolphins offense will be elite? No, I still think they have a myriad of questions in the receiving corps, and Willis is still unproven as a full-time starter, but schematically, their run game could be very fun. With all of the speed and run threats in the backfield, their offense could put a lot of nice stuff on tape, a promising sign for a team that's in year one of a rebuild.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    The Cleveland youth movementStop me if you've heard this before: the Browns might be bad, but their young guys are talented and can be built around. I know we've been on this ride before with Cleveland, but the biggest reason for hope on a team with one of the worst QB battles in the league is that all of their prized young guys are going to play significant reps. On offense, second-year RB Quinshon Judkins and TE Harold Fannin Jr. are the highlights, but rookie wideouts KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston have been tearing up camp for the Browns. Concepcion was the second of their first round picks (the other being LT Spencer Fano), and HC Todd Monken has found many ways to get him the ball, as well as Boston. The QB battle might look rough, but the young supporting cast should provide some fun moments.On defense, the young core of EDGE Jared Verse, DT Mason Graham, reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year LB Carson Schwesinger and S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren should provide consistent pop (even if they don't get sack production like they did last year). CB Denzel Ward should still remain one of the best CBs in the league, giving new DC Mike Rutenberg a bevy of tools in his arsenal. With Rutenberg coming from the Atlanta Falcons, I wonder if Cleveland leans more on pressure through scheme and simulated looks than on just lining up and winning. If so, you'll see a lot of youth and athleticism making plays.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    An offensive line that can be built aroundFor the Jets, I could've just expanded this to the entire offense (which we'll get to later), but I think their offensive line is on the verge of becoming a special unit. Which is what you should expect after spending three Day 1 or 2 picks on offensive linemen in the last three years. The trio of RT Armand Membou, LT Olu Fashanu and RG Joe Tippmann gives the Jets an athletic core on the offensive line, one that can play in both zone and gap schemes. Round that group out with Josh Myers and Dylan Parham, and you have a unit that can be very good very soon.The Jets' offense as a whole is one I'm cautiously keeping an eye on. I don't have much faith in OC Frank Reich, but the core is there for this offense not to be a bottom dweller in 2026. A receiving corps of Garrett Wilson, AD Mitchell, Mason Taylor and rookies Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper Jr. could be very fun to watch, with RBs Breece Hall and Braelon Allen in the backfield. New QB Geno Smith could find his mojo after a down year, but even if he's not what he was in Seattle, having a QB who is willing to test tight windows could elevate this offense a lot. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Bijan RobinsonBefore EDGE Jalon Walker tore his ACL and EDGE James Pearce Jr. got suspended for eight games, I would've put a defense that retains their defensive coordinator, Jeff Ulbrich (I do think their secondary is quietly becoming something special), but instead I'm going to go with one of the coolest players in the NFL, Bijan Robinson. Since entering the NFL, Robinson leads the NFL in touches, scrimmage yards and is sixth among all ball carriers in first downs or touchdowns per touch (min. 600 touches). The coolest part about Robinson is that he's not only able to make people miss but also run through contact at a high level. Robinson just got a big-time extension, and it was much deserved for being one of the best players in the league.
I'm excited to see how HC Kevin Stefanski continues to get Robinson the ball. The offense shouldn't change much from former playcaller Zac Robinson, plenty of wide zone with boot action off of it, but there will be many more under-center looks and designed downfield targets. The depth of the Falcons' receiver room isn't anything spectacular, so I still expect Robinson to be a feature in the passing game as well. This offseason hasn't been perfect for the Falcons, but Robinson is one of the few bright spots in what could be a rocky season for Atlanta.

title: Jannik Sinner injury: World No. 1 to miss U.S. Open with ongoing knee problem - CBS Sports
description: The reigning Wimbledon champion has not played since winning the title in London
body:
The reigning Wimbledon champion has not played since winning the title in London
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:52 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Jannik Sinner officially announced he was withdrawing from the 2026 U.S. Open on Friday, making it three consecutive grand slams in which one of the top two players in men's tennis -- Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz -- sat out due to injury. Sinner posted to social media on Friday morning that he was not going to be able to play in New York next week due to an ongoing knee issue. "Even though I have been working hard with my team and my medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete at the US Open this year," Sinner wrote. "We have been back on court in Monte Carlo over the last couple of days and have realized that I still need more time to recover from my right knee issue. I'm obviously very sad and disappointed, as New York has a special place in my heart. I was very much looking forward to coming back and playing in the electric atmosphere in front of the great fans there."Sinner withdrew from the Cincinnati Open earlier this month due to an injury to his right knee. In his efforts to ramp up in preparation for the U.S. Open, he realized he was not healthy enough to give it a go. Sinner's 2026 major season will come to a close with one grand slam title at Wimbledon, which was also the only grand slam final he reached. 
Sinner's withdrawal from the U.S. Open is a disappointing end to a frustrating year for the two top stars in men's tennis. Last year, Alcaraz and Sinner delivered three instant-classics in the finals at the French Open, Wimbledon and the U.S. Open. This year, Alcaraz missed the French Open and Wimbledon due to a wrist injury and Sinner will now miss the U.S. Open due to his knee, guaranteeing that fans go a full year without seeing the two dominant forces in men's tennis meet in a grand slam match. In Sinner's absence, French Open champion Alexander Zverev moving into the No. 1 seed in the draw while Alcaraz will take the No. 2 seed in his first start since April.
With Sinner out and Alcaraz shaking off the rust from nearly four months off the court, there may not be a better opportunity for one of the top American stars to snap the 23-year drought since the last American man won a grand slam title (Andy Roddick, 2003 U.S. Open).

title: WNBA MVP race: Can Caitlin Clark or Olivia Miles stop A'ja Wilson from running away with her third in a row? - CBS Sports
description: When Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson was named MVP last season, she became the first player in league history to win the honor four time
body:
When Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson was named MVP last season, she became the first player in league history to win the honor four times and joined Cynthia Cooper as the only players to go back-to-back. Now, Wilson is attempting to win her fifth MVP and become the only player to win the award three years in a row. Due to the 2026 FIBA World Cup, which will run from Sept. 4-13 in Berlin, the WNBA will pause from Aug. 31-Sept. 16. And so, while there's more than a month until the regular season comes to a close on Sept. 24, there are just over two weeks of regular season action remaining. In terms of games played, the season itself is more than three-fourths complete.Wilson is the overwhelming favorite to win MVP (-1100, per FanDuel), ahead of Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles -- an even bigger favorite for Rookie of the Year -- and Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark. As the regular season winds down, let's take a closer look at the MVP race and answer three big questions. 
Why is Wilson such a big favorite?Simply put, Wilson is having a historic season. She's averaging 25.9 points, 9.5 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 1.4 steals and two blocks on 51.8/40.5/86.1 shooting splits. Not only is she well on her way to a third consecutive scoring title, she's on pace to record the second-highest single-season scoring average ever, behind only her own mark of 26.9 points in 2024. Her 11 30-point games lead the league and are already tied for the fourth-most in a season. This would be just the second time in WNBA history that a player averaged at least 25 points, nine rebounds and two blocks in a season. The other was Wilson in 2024. Wilson also leads the league in blocks and is fourth in rebounds, and it should be no surprise that no other player is in the top four in the league in scoring, rebounding and blocks. Furthermore, the advanced stats love Wilson, who leads the league in both win shares (7.3) and RAPM (+5.7). 
The reigning champion Aces have not been at their best since the All-Star break, but still sit in third place at 25-13 thanks in large part to Wilson, who has carried the team on both sides of the ball. Notably, she has scored more than one-fourth of the Aces' points this season -- 908 of 3,443, 26.4% -- and her on/off splits are staggering:Wilson's StatusMin.Off. Rtg.Def. Rtg.Net Rtg.ON1,094118.2106.9+11.3OFF38698.4114.8-16.3Wilson's status as the reigning back-to-back MVP is impossible to ignore, but she's not coasting on her previous success. This is one of the best individual seasons in league history. Who has a chance to overtake Wilson?Wilson is likely going to win MVP, but there's still just enough of the season remaining that she doesn't have it completely locked up. Here are the current top five in MVP odds:A'ja Wilson: -1100Olivia Miles: +1000Caitlin Clark: +2700Kelsey Mitchell: +4000Paige Bueckers: +12500The Wings got a nice win Thursday, but they're still stuck in eighth place, so we can rule Bueckers out based on that alone. Mitchell has been awesome this season and is the best pure scorer in the league, but she doesn't make enough of an impact in other departments to win MVP. That leaves two players: Clark and Miles. Caitlin ClarkClark has had a fascinating season filled with incredible highs and pretty bad lows. She hit her first career game-winner, scored a career-high 45 points and has enough 20-point, 10-assist games this season alone (10) to be tied with Courtney Vandersloot for the league's all-time lead. (Clark has 20 such games for her career.)  On the flip side, she was pilloried early in the season for her defense, has gone through multiple shooting slumps, missed multiple weeks with a back injury after taking a retroactive Flagrant 2 from Alyssa Thomas and once again leads the league in turnovers. For the season, Clark is averaging a career-high 21.7 points and 8.3 assists. She's third in the league in scoring, leads the league in assists and is sixth in 3-pointers (90). No player in WNBA history has ever led the league in assists and finished in the top three in scoring, and Clark would also be the first player to average at least 20 points and eight assists. Clark is having a historic season in her own right, and is going to deservedly make First Team All-WNBA. But she has ultimately been too inconsistent to have a real chance at MVP. It also doesn't help her case that the Fever have a better net rating with her off the court this season: plus-4.1 net rating with Clark on and plus-13.3 net rating with Clark off. Olivia MilesIf anyone is going to overtake Wilson, Miles, who is having one of the best rookie campaigns ever and has helped lead the Lynx to the league's best record, has the best chance. Everyone knew about Miles' generational playmaking ability, but no one expected her to be at this level as a scorer and shooter -- especially right out of the gate. Miles is averaging 19.9 points, 4.7 rebounds, 6.2 assists and 1.3 steals on 50.3/40.7/87.2 shooting splits, leads all rookies in scoring, assists, steals and 3-pointers, and is eighth in the league in scoring and eighth in assists. She currently has the fourth-highest rookie scoring average in league history and the fifth-highest rookie assist average, and is on pace to surpass Clark for the highest rookie season points total. (Miles needs 74 points in Minnesota's final seven games.)On the advanced stats front, Miles is not far behind Wilson. She's third in both win shares (5.9) and RAPM (+4.6). The Lynx are also significantly worse without Miles on the floor: plus-13.4 net rating with Miles and plus-5.4 net rating without her. Miles' brilliance, particularly on the offensive end, is a major reason why the Lynx have far exceeded expectations this season. They lost six rotation players during the offseason, made no major free agent signings and Napheesa Collier underwent surgery on both ankles that kept her out until late July. And yet, the Lynx are four games ahead of every other team and are almost certainly going to be the No. 1 overall seed again. 
Miles has been the best player on the league's best team from start to finish. That may not be enough for her to become the first rookie since Parker to win MVP, but it's a very strong case. But what would it take for someone to overtake Wilson?As good as Clark and Miles have been this season, Wilson is still in firm control over the race. If Wilson's quest for five is to be delayed another season, one -- and likely multiple -- of the following scenarios would be necessary:Wilson suffers an injuryKnock on wood this will not happen, but if you're laying out a possible path for Clark, Miles or another candidate to win MVP, it has to be mentioned. Wilson herself benefited from this exact scenario last season. Napheesa Collier was the clear favorite for MVP until she sprained her ankle late in the season and missed multiple weeks, during which time Wilson and the Aces began a historic run to close the campaign. Wilson's play falls off dramaticallyWilson is one of the most consistent players in the league. She's scored at least 20 points in 28 of her 35 games this season, and has never been under 15 points; she's grabbed at least seven rebounds in 25 of 35 games, and has been under five rebounds just four times; she has blocked multiple shots in 26 of 35 games, and has failed to block a shot just seven times.
The odds that Wilson's production suddenly falls off a cliff are near zero. The Aces collapseWith their win and the Indiana Fever's loss on Thursday, the Aces moved back into third place. While playoff seeding is not the deciding factor for MVP votes, it does play a major part. There have only been four instances in league history when a player won MVP while playing for a team that did not have a top-four overall record: Candace Parker in 2008 (5th), Lauren Jackson in 2007 (7th), Sheryl Swoopes in 2005 (5th) and Jackson in 2003 (t-5th). If the Aces fall apart down the stretch and slide into fifth or sixth place, that would be a big blow to Wilson's campaign. But just as it's extremely unlikely that Wilson would suddenly stop producing, there's no world in which the Aces collapse. In fact, it's far more likely they run the table and jump the Valkyries for second place. They only play lottery teams the rest of the way and have the easiest remaining schedule in the league (opponent winning percentage of .273)
Another candidate goes on a crazy runIn addition to needing Wilson to falter, any candidate hoping to overtake her will have to play lights out down the stretch to not only boost their numbers (and potentially their team's playoff seeding), but make a statement to voters.

title: Commissioner Cathy Engelbert slams 'haters' using WNBA to 'sow divisiveness' in debate over trans athletes - CBS Sports
description: 'We're being the center of political football for people who have never watched the WNBA,' she said
body:
'We're being the center of political football for people who have never watched the WNBA,' she said
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:55 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert made a public appearance Thursday alongside Dallas Wings CEO Greg Bibb ahead of Dallas' 91-85 win over Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever, and called out the "haters" who are trying to "sow divisiveness" around the league. Over the last month, the WNBA has become a battleground for the debate about transgender athletes after Fever guard Sophie Cunningham made a series of comments. "People are trying to use the league to sow divisiveness," Engelbert said. "We're being the center of political football for people who have never watched the WNBA, never have written about the WNBA or reported on the WNBA.""There's always going to be haters out there, and we denounce it," Engelbert continued. "But that's what happens when you have made it as a legitimate sports media and entertainment product."
Cunningham's comments spark debateIn an ESPN profile last month, Cunningham said that she wants to "protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men." Later, she doubled down prior to the Fever's win over the Connecticut Sun on July 22. "I said what I said. I think it's kind of common sense," Cunningham said. "And I think I'll always believe in that. I think it's really important to protect children, and that's little girls who are also involved in that category. I stand on what I said."Cunningham added that she doesn't "dislike anyone" and that there's "room to love everyone." She continued, "I'm also there to love biological women, and I think that there are rights that need to be protected. And, like I said, I'm gonna stand true to that. I'll never falter in my beliefs in that. But I have never once stated that I hated the trans community."
The WNBA has never had a transgender player and does not have a public policy about transgender participation. The new collective bargaining agreement states simply that, "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." 
        
            
                WNBA denounced 'bad-faith' actors amid fight over trans participation. Now it needs to lead the conversation
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Recently, former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White "declared" for the 2027 WNBA Draft by claiming that they now identify as women. Earlier this month, the WNBA put together a task force to discuss the issue and issued a statement that read, in part, "We will approach these important conversations thoughtfully and in alignment with the values of our league. There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA, and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others."
A series of incidents involving fansIn the time since Cunningham's comments, there have been a series of incidents both before and during WNBA games. There have been multiple rallies in support of Cunningham outside of arenas in Seattle, Portland, Minneapolis and Dallas.Additionally, Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton approached multiple teenage fans who were sitting courtside wearing shirts supporting Cunningham during a Fever-Storm game last month and directed expletives at them. Keaton was suspended for the next five home games and fined an undisclosed amount. 

        
            
                WNBA suspends Storm co-owner for confronting fans supporting Sophie Cunningham after trans athletes comments
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"We are aware one of our co-owners made comments to two fans in attendance at last night's game. We apologize that this happened," Storm majority owner Ginny Gilder said in a statement at the time. "Everyone who attends a Storm game deserves to feel welcome, and we remain committed to creating an inclusive environment where every fan is treated with respect."Cunningham called Keaton's behavior "truly embarrassing" and said it "shows the type of leader she is."Most recently, WNBA security made multiple fans cover shirts with messaging related to transgender athletes during the Fever's win over the Dream in Atlanta. The league later released a statement saying, "The WNBA is aware of interactions at (Sunday) night's game in Atlanta in which fans were asked by league security to cover their shirts. This should not have happened."

title: Drafting Rounds 1-2 RBs is the secret recipe for 2026 Fantasy leagues - CBS Sports
description: Jacob Gibbs thinks we may have unlocked a cheat code to drafting your 2026 Fantasy Football rosters
body:
Jacob Gibbs thinks we may have unlocked a cheat code to drafting your 2026 Fantasy Football rosters

        The first two rounds of your 2026 Fantasy Football drafts could produce multiple league-winning draft picks at the running back position and it appears this is more defined than we've seen in past years. This range of Fantasy Football drafts produces league-winners at a really high (relatively speaking) rate. And in 2026, this range of drafts is dominated by the RB position. What is one to do when on the clock and staring at a list of awesome running backs?! Let's sort through the early-round RB league-winning candidates.I'm going to profile each back for Fantasy purposes -- offering my perception of their ceiling, floor, and stability. Hopefully this helps you in some way. It's arbitrary; I made it up. I've ruminated on potential outcomes for these players a lot, though, so hopefully this is an effective way for my thoughts to resonate.Here's how I understand this concept:Ceiling rating - if the player hits a 75th percentile (or better) outcome, how impactful is it on a scale of 1-100?Floor rating - how concerned am I by the possibility of the player hitting a 25th percentile (or worse) outcome?Stability rating - on a scale of 1-100, how impactful is variability in this player's outlook?High number = goodHigh ceiling rating = Lots of upsideHigh floor rating = Lots of warm fuzzy feelings of (probably false) security when I click this player's name
High stability rating = the outcome feels more predictable. The path to a "good" outcome feels wide and easy to navigate. Please do not toy with us today, chaos.Another way to think about this stability rating: how many factors outside of the individual's control are they relying on to shape their outcome? Furthermore, how reliable do those factors feel? A player with many unreliable factors available to influence their outcome will have a low stability rating.If we simulated the NFL season 100 times, the 25 best outcomes would represent 75th-100th percentile outcomes. Those outcomes represent the player's "ceiling." The 25 worst outcomes would represent the 1st-25th percentile outcomes. Those outcomes represent the player's "floor."
What might these outcomes look like? How might a player arrive at such an outcome? We obviously don't have those answers, but we can speculate on them and aim to place our best bets.James Cook (my RB4)Ceiling rating - 89 (out of 100)Floor rating - 75 (I'm a little concerned about the workload)Stability rating - 85James Cook gets to his ceiling outcome through an expanded receiving role and continued dominance on the ground. Cook hits his floor outcome as a result of diminished offensive line play, or wear and tear catching up to him after a massive 2025 workload.
Chase Brown (my RB5)Ceiling rating - 87Floor rating - 90Stability rating - 80Chase Brown gets to his ceiling outcome through an eruption season from the Cincinnati Bengals offense. Brown hits his floor outcome as a result of skill issue (pass protection has at times led to him losing reps when backfield teammates were healthy) or Cincy's offense not playing up to expectation.Ashton Jeanty (my RB6)Ceiling rating - 86Floor rating - 80Stability rating - 82 (I know it feels high. He's a young player with massive organizational investment who has already shown an ability to handle a gargantuan workload)Ashton Jeanty gets to his ceiling outcome through improved offensive line play and usage maximization within Klint Kubiak's plan. Jeanty hits his floor outcome as a result of skill issue (he had such a low explosive play rate last year - easily reasoned away with offensive environment excuses, but still - we need to see improvement here for him to deliver Fantasy efficiency) or offensive ecosystem dysfunction.
Jonathan Taylor (my RB7)Ceiling rating - 91Floor rating - 69Stability rating - 60Jonathan Taylor gets to his ceiling outcome through positive game scripts allowing the Colts to lean on the ground game in a return to form for the offense. He also offers unique "any given play" ability that can make him a weekly Fantasy winner. JT hits his floor outcome as a result of Indy's offense underperforming, the defense struggling to the point that the Colts have to take to the air more than preferred, or wear and tear simply catching up to him.Oct 21, 2024; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Los Angeles Chargers offensive tackle Rashawn Slater (70) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images 
                                                                    Mark J. Rebilas
                                                            Omarion Hampton (my RB8)Ceiling rating - 90 (JT gets the edge because of true bell-cow dominance. Hampton's ceiling outcome feels similar to Cook's)Floor rating - 60Stability rating - 66Omarion Hampton gets to his ceiling outcome through an massive touchdown production within a high-powered Chargers offense. He also offers efficiency upside through explosive play potential. Hampton hits his floor outcome as a result of skill issue (he's the most unproven RB being selected in this range), backfield competition, or L.A.'s offense not living up to hype.
De'Von Achane (my RB9)Ceiling rating - 89Floor rating - 72Stability rating - 30De'Von Achane gets to his ceiling outcome through explosive plays, a surprising positive performance from Miami's offense, or a uniquely large receiving role within an offense lacking proven receiving options. Achane hits his floor outcome as a result of wear and tear, poor coaching, or lack of space for his skills to shine with defenses focusing all attention on him.Kenneth Walker (my RB10)Ceiling rating - 88Floor rating - 63Stability rating - 55Kenneth Walker gets to his ceiling outcome through an expanded receiving role and improved rushing efficiency behind a better offensive line. Walker hits his floor outcome as a result of splitting backfield reps, lack of receiving role, Kansas City's offense underperforming, or wear and tear becoming a problem once again.
                                                                    Imagn Images
                                                            Derrick Henry (my RB11)Ceiling rating - 87Floor rating - 79Stability rating - 77Derrick Henry gets to his ceiling outcome through an offensive eruption in Baltimore. He also could see an expanded receiving role. And, of course, explosive play ability always offers Henry upside to produce top-end efficiency. Henry hits his floor outcome as a result of diminished offensive line play, overhyped coaching, or wear and tear catching up to him.
Saquon Barkley (my RB12)Ceiling rating - 87Floor rating - 72Stability rating - 70Saquon Barkley gets to his ceiling outcome through a return to health for his offensive line, an injection of energy from a new play-caller, or better luck converting red zone touchdowns. He also might offer explosive play upside once again. Barkley hits his floor outcome as a result of offensive line injuries, overhyped coaching, or wear and tear catching up to him.If you wanna hear me talk through my thoughts on each of these backs in more detail, here's an hour on Beyond the Box Score! I think I'm going to move Derrick Henry ahead of Kenneth Walker after this practice.

This ruling will only trigger more legal battles in the coming weeks

        The Tenth Circuit has granted the NCAA's stay request in the Wisne vs. NCAA lawsuit. That means qualifying players from the Class of 2022 are once again ineligible unless they have already been granted temporary restraining orders or injunctions.Earlier this summer, Colorado District Judge Charlotte Sweeney ruled that some members of the 2022 class could be granted a fifth year of eligibility. Despite a later clarification that athletes who signed NFL contracts would be ineligible for a return to college football, rookies across the league have been exploring NCAA comebacks.On Wednesday, former LSU standout and current Tampa Bay Buccaneer Jack Pyburn and 15 other athletes were granted a temporary restraining order by a Louisiana judge. Because Pyburn and the other 15 players have their own temporary restraining order, the Tenth Circuit's ruling doesn't affect them, and they are eligible for a return to college football.
While this new ruling in Wisne vs. NCAA may be a victory for the NCAA, it will trigger another wave of lawsuits as other members of the 2022 class seek their own temporary restraining orders and injuctions.
This is about to get particularly interesting as the NFL regular season approaches. With roster cut-down day set for Aug. 30, more rookies on the fringes could turn their attention back to the college ranks instead of fighting for roster spots at the pro level. If that happens, they may take legal action in hopes of getting one more year of eligibility.We've already seen a slew of athletes score victories in that department. Recently, Arizona State defensive back and All-Big 12 honoree Myles Rowser was granted a temporary restraining order that not only granted him a fifth year of eligibility but also allowed him to enter the transfer portal.
Other players -- like Indiana edge rushers Stephen Daley and Kellar Wyatt -- have announced their return on the strength of the Colorado eligibility ruling. They are now ineligible for the moment, but they are among countless other players who could take legal action to get a temporary restraining order or injunction of their own.

title: Candid Coaches: Who will be the best college hoops team in 2026-27? - CBS Sports
description: Matt Norlander and Gary Parrish surveyed nearly 100 coaches to provide the first big preseason college hoops poll
body:
Matt Norlander and Gary Parrish surveyed nearly 100 coaches to provide the first big preseason college hoops poll
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:54 am ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Welcome back to another year of CBS Sports' Candid Coaches feature. College basketball insiders Gary Parrish and Matt Norlander surveyed nearly 100 men's Division I coaches in the thick of the offseason; as always, interviewees were given the promise of anonymity in a swap for honest and enlightening answers on a medley of topics. Be it some of the most high-profile names in the game or assistants at low-major programs, Norlander and Parrish spanned the sport to get a wide range of feedback. This year's survey had nine questions; this is No. 3 of the group.  The 2026-27 preseason college basketball coaches' poll has arrived! With all due respect to the USA Today poll that's considered the official one on behalf of college coaches, we're not making you wait until October to get a look at what these guys think about the best teams. Plus, ours is much more representative of the sport. Way more coaches vote in our questionnaire every summer. We're coming off one of the five best seasons of the 21st century as far as I'm concerned. The sport's offseason has been a predictable mess, but the product on the floor remains terrific. Which team should take up the top spot? Who is most likely to spend the most time at No. 1 from November through March? Nine schools got votes from the nearly 100 coaches we surveyed. Here's the return. 
    Which team will be the best in 2026-27?     Other schools receiving votes: Arizona, Louisville, Michigan State, Texas                    Quotes that stood out                       On Florida    "I think there's no excuse for Florida to not sit at No. 1 most of the year. 80% of scoring back with three true frontcourt monsters that probably eclipse most teams' total salaries by themselves." "My heart wants to say Tennessee because coach Barnes is due a Final Four run, but my brain says Florida can and will probably be stupid-good this year. Like, 30-plus-win good and back to the championship game. Too many guys who have been there before and a coaching staff that knows what their coach wants and needs! How many programs at that level can say that? And have the horses?""They have the best frontcourt in college baskeball. Hard to go against their physicality and competitive spirit, as they wear teams down over 40 minutes. Boogie Fland will be much improved and more consistent in Year 2." "Just so much coming back, adding Aberdeen (if cleared) is a missing piece at guard they needed last year that already knows the system. Massive upgrade over (Xaivian) Lee. I do think they will have to deal with unreasonable expectations and we will see if there's a such thing as a group staying together for too long?""Not even close, in my opinion. The combination of great returning players along with Todd Golden and Carlin Hartman at the helm is unmatched. Aberdeen being somewhat cleared to play a fifth year is just icing on the cake. Really tough schedule obviously, but I could see them dropping only four games before SEC tournament starts in March."                    On Duke    "Because they get the best players and the most talent. They came close the last couple of years and then f----ing went out and spent big again. When you're paying guys so much money like they are, and you're getting them there, they should be great.""Can't believe I'm saying this, but if Duke's frontcourt is good AT ALL, they are in pole position.""I'm buying on Duke. Think they have the best blend of returning talent and acquisition. Plus, the way their year has ended the last two years in a collapse, they're due for some good luck."    On Tennessee   "I really like Tennessee's roster and I respect how they do things. If the portal class buys into the physical paint dominance that they have possessed in the past, they could win it all. I love their transfer additions and I think they fit well together.""They develop their players, they attack you offensively in different ways, and they defend as well as anyone. They continue to add talent and appear to have great depth. I have to believe this is the year Rick Barnes gets them to the Final Four." 
        
            
                College basketball transfer portal five-for-five tracker: Grading each move in unparalleled free agency window
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
On Illinois"Illinois would be my choice if they had reliable point guard play. I'm not sold that Quentin Coleman can be the point guard they need as a freshman though. Florida would be the favorite for me. Most proven and they've done it before.""Illinois will be the best team in the country. They have skill, toughness and chemistry. Brad Underwood knows how to win with this group. Plus, it looks like the players actually like each other from the outside looking in. Chemistry matters in this landscape."    On Arizona   "If the fifth-year guys get cleared I'm going with Arizona. If the rule doesn't happen, then I'd lean toward Florida or UConn. Both programs have a strong core of returning players that have produced deep NCAA Tournament runs, and they understand what it takes to win in March. Experience and talent matters, [those teams] have plenty of both."                   The takeaway                   Florida winning, and by a big margin, was no surprise. The Gators will be the widespread pick atop every preseason poll you'll find this fall. Todd Golden is probably overseeing the most loaded roster he'll ever have as a college coach. And I say that while acknowledging the 36-4 squad with a First Team All-American (Walter Clayton Jr.) that won a national title a little more than 17 months ago. That Gators crew was reallllllllly good. Got a 1-seed and won the SEC in the same season that the SEC was the best league of any in college hoops history. Awesome team. This season's roster can be better if it maxes out.It has three starters from that title team — and they're all two years older. This team has the player that coaches voted will be the best in college basketball, Thomas Haugh, who turned down being a probable lottery pick to return as college basketball's highest-paid player (by far). National defensive player of the year Rueben Chinyelu is back, as is Alex Condon, who was (misguidedly) a preseason All-American last year. Boogie Fland should improve at the 2, and it seems like Denzel Aberdeen's eligibility case for a fifth season has a good shot of winning out. (Aberdeen was also on that title-winning team.) 
Florida brings back 81.8% of its points from last season, which is the fourth-most by any 1-seed in the past 24 years. In total, 11 players who suited up for Golden in 2025-26 will be back. There isn't another team with this kind of retention at the high-major level for this season, and it's why UF is the obvious choice for preseason No. 1. As for some of the others that received votes ... — Duke being the clear-cut No. 2 makes sense. Jon Scheyer's average KenPom finish the past three years: 3.7. While Florida will have the strongest roster, Duke has a good case at having the deepest. Wisconsin transfer John Blackwell is expected to lead the team in scoring, Patrick Ngongba should move into a huge role as one of the best bigs in the country, and the tantalizing guy to watch is 17-year-old Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje. If he flourishes with the talent around him, Duke will again strut its way to a No. 1 seed.— How about Rick Barnes' Tennessee team coming in third place? Barnes' reputation in college basketball circles also helped his cause; a lot of guys are rooting for him to make a second Final Four. I'm high on the Vols. This squad should have the best offense Barnes has rostered since he got to Knoxville more than a decade ago. Tennessee spent north of $15 million to break the Elite Eight ceiling. I like its chances to fight with Florida atop the SEC. 
— Dan Hurley's Huskies rightfully got some run after making a third title game in four years while bringing back Braylon Mullins and Silas Demary Jr. That's one of the best backcourts in college basketball. Seton Hall transfer big Najai Hines (who's gotten really good reviews in the offseason) will be the guy who determines if UConn can again be a force in March.— I thought Illinois would get a couple more votes than it did, but some of our surveying did take place amid the news that David Mirkovic required surgery for a foot injury in early August. The Illini had the No. 2 offense in college hoops last season and should be able to repeat that level of efficiency with so many minutes returning.— Arizona getting a few No. 1 votes says a lot about Tommy Lloyd's reputation. Keep in mind, he's won 148 games, the most of any coach to start a career in their first five seasons. Louisville's massive spending spree has a few coaches believing Pat Kelsey will have everything he needs to bring the Cardinals to the Final Four. The thinking was similar with Texas, which has broken the bank to get Sean Miller a squad capable of beating anyone. The Longhorns have one of my favorite transfers of 2026 in David Punch. And thanks to Michigan State potentially having the best player in the country in Jeremy Fears Jr. (along with some other vets sticking around in East Lansing), Sparty got two votes from coaches.
Best team not to receive at least one vote? I think Virginia's probably the pick. Ryan Odom had a 3-seed last season and is returning a good chunk of that roster to battle against Duke and Louisville atop the ACC.Previously in 2026 Candid Coaches ...  • Do you support 2026 seniors being grandfathered into the five-in-five rule?  • Who will be the best player for the 2026-27 season?

body:
Kai Spears, a former walk-on basketball player at Alabama, was awarded $9.25 million in a defamation case against the New York Times this week.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026

    11:46 am ET
                        
                •

                Getty Images
            
            

    
        An Alabama jury awarded $9.25 million in damages to former Crimson Tide basketball player Kai Spears on Thursday after an eight-person jury found the New York Times defamed him by incorrectly reporting that he was at the scene of a fatal shooting.The jury ruled in favor of Spears after the Times wrote in 2023 that he was a passenger in a car involved in the death of 23-year-old Jamea Harris, which he denied after the report came out. The Times reported that the person had spoken, "on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive matters." "I have one thing to say — the report in the New York Times was 100% inaccurate and the writer had complete disregard for the truth," Spears said in a statement in 2023. "I am trying to process and cope with these false statements that somehow have been published and then seen by so many. So thankful to Alabama Athletics for refuting it on my behalf."More than anything, I remain completely heartbroken by the tragic death that occurred that night."
Spears, who began his college basketball career at Alabama as a walk-on, transferred to Marshall in 2024, where he spent the last two seasons. He transferred to Division II West Liberty this offseason.

title: How 'The Bat King' created hundreds of custom looks for MLB Players' Weekend - CBS Sports
description: Bat manufacturer Victus and artist Bruce Tatem are making more than 400 custom bats that MLB players will be usin
body:
Bat manufacturer Victus and artist Bruce Tatem are making more than 400 custom bats that MLB players will be using this weekend
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:36 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Major League Baseball's Players' Weekend begins Friday, an annual event meant to celebrate the athletes "beyond the bases." Over the years, we've seen players wear off-the-wall jerseys with nicknames on the back and customized cleats, bats and gloves. This Players' Weekend, MLB has seen more than 400 submissions of customized bats, more than ever.A large portion of the bats are supplied by Victus, a bat manufacturer that began in New Jersey in 2012. CBS Sports spoke to Doug Trimble, the company's operations manager, about what we'll see this coming Players' Weekend, as well as some of the customized bats we've seen in the past.Gavin Sheets of the Padres will have man's best friend on his bat this weekend. 
                                                                    Victus
                                                            First things first, the art on every single bat is customized by one person. "We have an in-house artist, his name is Bruce Tatem, he goes by 'The Bat King,'" said Trimble. "He hand-paints all those bats. They're completely airbrushed. It's a common misconception that these come out of a machine. He's doing probably over 400 custom bats for Players' Weekend."We do a bunch around jewel events. We did a ton of stuff around the All-Star Game, the Home Run Derby, (Bryce) Harper's corn bat that he used in the Field of Dreams game, and then this weekend you'll see them all over the place." 
The Bat King's Instagram account is a treasure trove of the bats he's made, from Juan Soto to James Wood, as well as videos of him creating his art.

Often, Trimble said, the players aren't quite sure what they want to do yet, but Victus will work with them through team personnel. "Sometimes we internally come up with something creative for them -- if it's something they're known for, a moment that's already happened, a correlation with something that we think would be cool storytelling," Trimble told CBS Sports. "Half of it is the players reaching out if they want something specific. We'll give some players some options to pick from as well. If they don't have a specific idea, they could choose from a select amount of custom bats we've provided the clubhouse manager." 
MLB must approve all customized bats, ideally by a deadline, but Trimble admitted that his company has gotten requests as late as this week."An idea will pop in their head and they'll just remember that it's Players' Weekend and send us three ideas they wanna do," Trimble said. "Or they just got new cleats and they want the bat to go with the cleats or something like that. A lot of it, honestly, is last minute, so (Tatem)'s in the heat of it right now."Victus is supplying hundreds of custom bats for 2026 Players Weekend. 
                                                                    Victus
                                                            Some ideas are rejected, he conceded, but typically over licensing issues rather than subject matter.
"We've gotten stuff rejected before, and it's usually stuff that is too close to other company IPs," Trimble said. "Like, a lot of players just want this brand on the bat or a bat that looks like a soda can (like a Mountain Dew can). If it's stuff that's completely third-party branding, MLB will nix that." As for any favorites, there are a few viral moments that baseball fans will likely remember. Phillies infielder Bryson Stott swung a pencil at the 2023 Little League Classic. 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            "The first time the pencil hit the field, Bryson Stott used that in the Little League Classic, and it just went insane, viral across the whole nation," Trimble said. "That one was so cool just because it just looks like a jumbo pencil on TV. It looks like the actual object, so it was putting people in a craze. They thought it was edited because it looked so real. That was the first time something felt iconic." 
Trimble also bragged about Bobby Witt Jr.'s Pablo Sanchez bat, from the video game Backyard Baseball, which the Royals star used to hit a home run.
As for some of the best players to work with? "Julio Rodriguez always gives us cool ideas, Bryson Stott always gives good ideas, and he's great about using the custom stuff," Trimble said. "Obviously, Bryce Harper is all about it, the storytelling, and he likes custom stuff for the moment and stuff that correlates for the moment that the fans can engage with, like the corn bat at Field of Dreams -- stuff that's completely on brand that will ultimately bring kids and maybe people who aren't fans to the game. Things that hit social media. That's the cool part about Players' Weekend. It brings people to watch even if they aren't usually watching baseball, and it's a new thing that they can look at and interact with."  The bats, by far, are the viral success of Players' Weekend, and we have Victus and The Bat King to thank for many of them.

        The European season is officially underway, and between this weekend and next, the biggest European leagues will come back, and after a massive World Cup summer, plenty of people want to figure out how to keep the soccer party going and what teams to support around the world. From an accessibility standpoint, they can be some of the easier sides to keep an eye on in the global game, while also having names that you may recognize while getting into soccer. And for 24/7 coverage of all the action, don't miss CBS Sports Golazo Network, which is with you every step of the way.England Root for Arsenal if: You enjoy a front-runner and defensive soccer. England's defending champions have exciting players like Bukayo Saka and Christos Tzolis, but this is a team built on defense.Root for Manchester City if: The "Erling Haaland song" is still stuck in your head. It was the World Cup of the Norwegian, and he will score plenty of goals playing for the club this season.Root for Aston Villa if: You enjoy marching to the beat of your own drum. You kind of blinked, and Villa were in the Champions League, and this season, without Morgan Rogers, it will be tough to replicate their success, but that's why we play the games, and Unai Emery is a great manager.Root for Liverpool if: You like LeBron James or the Boston Red Sox, since one of Liverpool's ownership groups, RedBird Capital (which is also involved in AC Milan and Toulouse), has LeBron James' involvement, while the other group involved, Fenway Sports Group, owns the Red Sox. And they may be in for a bounce-back season.Root for Tottenham if: Chaos is your thing. Tottenham were almost relegated in consecutive seasons, and now they're back to pushing for European soccer, but after not signing a single attacker so far this summer, a lot of pressure is on Roberto De Zerbi's management.Root for Chelsea if: You think Xabi Alonso was unfairly sacked by Real Madrid and you enjoy chippy chips. All faith in the Blues is tied to a combination of backing their manager and ensuring that their french fries-loving midfielder, Cole Palmer, can get back to the top of his own game.Root for Manchester United if:  History matters. In the Premier League era, no team has more Premier League titles than Manchester United, and under Michael Carrick, the Red Devils are looking to get back to their glory days.
        
            
                Predicting the full Premier League table: Arsenal on top as new Man City era begins without Pep Guardiola
                
                    James Benge                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
ItalyRoot for Juventus or Milan if: Country Roads and the United States men's national team gave you the soccer bug during the World Cup. Weston McKennie, and Christian Pulisic can be seen on Paramount+ all season long.Root for Napoli if: You're a fan of glow-ups. Every player who heads to Napoli starts moving differently as they set foot in one of Europe's most unlikely recent success stories, and the soccer isn't half bad either.Root for Inter if: You like teams that do more with less. This isn't a big spending club, but Inter have been able to compete with Europe's best at a fraction of the budget.
        
            
                Five World Cup talents to watch in Serie A: England's Djed Spence, Christian Pulisic's new teammate and more
                
                    Francesco Porzio                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
GermanyRoot for Bayern Munich if: You like machines. Bayern are going to show up, score plenty of goals with trademark German efficiency, in no small part thanks to England's star striker, Harry Kane, and they'll be among the contenders for a Champions League title under Vincent Kompany.Root for Borussia Dortmund if: You want to see the stars of tomorrow, today. From Robert Lewandowski and Marco Reus to Alexander Isak, Jude Bellingham, and Erling Haaland, plenty of stars have made a stop in the Black and Yellow. They even have another Bellingham in Jobe, if you still have a Jude jersey, alongside a young American winger, Mathis Albert.FranceRoot for Paris Saint-Germain if: You believe in the merits of the Ewing theory that a team plays better after losing their superstar. Life after Kylian Mbappe has been great for PSG, who will now chase their third consecutive Champions League title while also being one of the most fun teams in the world.Root for Marseille if: You enjoy France but hate PSG, their historic rivals are also an option.Spain Root for Barcelona if: Spain's World Cup win entranced you. Now with Rodri, formerly of Manchester City, in the mix, the core of the Spanish national team will suit up for Barcelona as the defending LaLiga champions look to win the Champions League for the first time since 2015.Root for Real Madrid if: You want chaos of a higher order. The Jose Mourinho experience has a little bit of everything and always has the chance of an explosion in his press conferences. Add in excellent players such as Jude Bellingham, Vinicius Junior and Kylian Mbappe, and it'll be quite a time as Real tries to get back to the top of LaLiga.Root for Atletico Madrid if: You enjoy physical soccer. Diego Simeone is a master of the dark arts, and it rubs off on his teams, making Atleti underdogs who can still make things happen in the league.Root for Villarreal if: The Yellow Submarine entrances you. Not only does the club have one of the best nicknames in soccer, but it also has ex-Green Bay Packer wide receiver Antonio Freeman's son, Alex Freeman, a right back for all the NFL and USMNT fans out there to keep an eye on.

 	🤯 Five things to know Friday Multiple NFL players will put their names in the college football transfer portal. It defies everything the NCAA has ever stood for, but, yes, you read that right. Harden, after the Seahawks waived him on Monday, declared his intention to enter the portal and seek another year of college football. There could be a wave of portal entrances, and we have our eyes on Diego Pavia, who is no stranger to eligibility battles. College football staffers are split on whether this is a good thing or not, while SEC commissioner Greg Sankey is very much not a fan.De'Zhaun Stribling was the star of Thursday's preseason action. The spotlight heading into Week 2 of the NFL preseason was on Fernando Mendoza, as the No. 1 overall draft pick took over the Raiders' starting quarterback duties. But after he threw a pick-six and had an otherwise uneventful day, it was the 49ers rookie wide receiver who jumped into the limelight. Stribling, a second-round pick from Ole Miss, showed off quite the connection with signal-callers Brock Purdy and Mac Jones and hauled in four catches for 46 yards across two drives. James Harden will return to the Cavaliers. Whether he would re-sign with Cleveland was less of a question than the size of his contract. It took a couple of months to get there, but he ultimately came to terms with the team on a three-year, $97 million deal that includes a player option for 2028-29 and a trade kicker. Harden will become the eighth NBA player to surpass $500 million in career earnings by the end of his contract. At 37, this figures to be the final long-term deal of Harden's career.Huge fights broke out across NFL joint practices. On one hand, this is nothing new. Tempers flare in these settings every year. But at the same time, some of these skirmishes are crossing the line. There are harmless scuffles like the one involving Joe Burrow. And then there are the fights that marred two other practices. But there are 30 teams in the NBA, and not all of them are run so smoothly. Our Sam Quinn defined the NBA's worst front offices as those who operate without a bigger-picture vision.
